content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INC-2026-0421 triggered - abnormal memory growth observed in paged-attention KV allocator on us-west-2. Symptoms: repeated CUDA OOMs, pod crashes, node flaps. Please triage.

Maya L: spotted multiple runtime pods entering CrashLoop with `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` starting ~11:40 UTC. Error rate on /v1/generate rose to ~9%.

Alex P: heap/allocator logs indicate progressive page fragmentation. Not a single oversized allocation, more like retained partial pages across many sessions.

Maya L: paste from pod log: 
```
2026-04-21T11:39:58Z runtime: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
allocator/paged.c:317 allocate_page(): total_pages=256k, free_pages=1.2k, retained_pages=205k
kv: page_ref_counts: high_water=67 -> leak suspected
```

Samir K: could be the rotation prune change from last sprint. Suspect prune misses when sessions terminate mid-rotate, leaving page refs.

Maya L: confirmed rotation pruning enabled in prod. Hypothesis: race in prune path where session cache cleanup isn't synced with rotation pointer updates. Leads to silent retention and fragmentation until OOM.

Rachel G: customer impact: /v1/generate and /v1/chat sporadic 502/503 and `internal_error: cuda_alloc_fail`. Top affected tenants by logs: ten-acme-prod, ten-data-labs, ten-sandbox-research (best-effort). Notifying support for outreach.

Alex P: immediate mitigations to run now: 1) trigger KV eviction for entries older than 12h, 2) throttle long-context requests (set max_tokens=1024 on generation routes), 3) staggered rolling restarts of runtime pods on affected nodes, 4) enable routing fallback to CPU model for non-critical traffic.

Maya L: executing eviction: `POST /admin/kv/evict?older_than=12h&force=true`.

deploy-bot: @Maya L launched job evict-1766543210 (job id: e9c1). Progress: 22% - cleaning ~4.5M slot references.

Alex P: I prepared a runtime patch that tightens prune refcount handling in branch `fix/kv-prune-fix`. If eviction doesn't reduce fragmentation, we'll canary that patch.

Maya L: eviction finished. Observed immediate per-pod RSS drop ~28% on many pods, but three nodes still hit OOM during pod startup. Looks like some nodes had higher retained working sets.

TJ: cordoning and draining two problematic instances in us-west-2: i-0aa11bb22cc33dd44 and i-0ee99ff88gg77hh66. Commands executed: 
```
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-28-76
kubectl drain ip-10-0-28-76 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
aws ec2 stop-instances --instance-ids i-0aa11bb22cc33dd44 i-0ee99ff88gg77hh66
```

Ops-OnCall: preparing a status page entry. ETA for broader mitigation ~40-70 minutes. Draft: "Intermittent memory allocation failures affecting inference endpoints in us-west-2; we are rolling mitigations (cache eviction, targeted restarts, runtime patch rollout)."

Samir K: plan for canary if needed: deploy `fix/kv-prune-fix` to 2 pods per AZ, monitor allocator frag_metric and RSS for 20-30m, then roll gradually.

Maya L: applied canary to runtime-prod-usw2-a-1 and runtime-prod-usw2-c-2. Canary metrics: frag_index dropped from ~0.91 -> ~0.14 on patched pods.

incident-bot: Node i-0aa11bb22cc33dd44 reported reboot - reduced crash loops from 42 to 6. Autorestart handled.

Maya L: performing controlled restarts across remaining runtime pods at 20s spacing. Patch now at ~50% of fleet.

Rachel G: finalizing status page text to include observed error codes `cuda_alloc_fail`, 502/503 responses, and list of probable impacted tenants. Will publish after 25m stable metrics.

Alex P: enabling routing fallback for non-SLA traffic to cpu-quant model via routing policy `fallback_to_cpu=true` for tiers free/standard.

Maya L: collecting per-pod allocator diagnostics for the ticket. Command used to capture stats: 
```
kubectl exec runtime-prod-usw2-a-1 -- /bin/sh -c "/opt/runtime/bin/kv-dump-stats --text" > /tmp/kv-dump-a1.txt
```

Samir K: root cause tracked to a race in rotation prune where a session termination event can skip decrementing page refcount when the rotation pointer moves. Patch ensures atomic refcount decrement and adds a safety path that reclaims pages when frag_ratio > 0.65.

deploy-bot: Hotfix `hotfix/kv-prune-atomic` built and pushed, canary roll scheduled.

Maya L: memory and frag metrics on hotfix canaries and restarted nodes look stable. Error rate on /v1/generate decreased from 9% -> 0.6% within 30 minutes.

Ops-OnCall: preparing shift handoff notes. Summary to incoming oncall:
- Incident INC-2026-0421: KV allocator rotation prune race caused retained refs -> fragmentation -> OOMs in us-west-2.
- Actions taken: aggressive KV eviction, node drains/restarts, patch canaries + hotfix rollout, temporary routing fallbacks, request token cap.
- Impact: elevated 502/503 and cuda_alloc failures on generation/chat routes; affected tenants (best-effort) listed above. No data leak detected.
- Next steps: complete full rollout, monitor frag_ratio and RSS for 2 hours, run synthetic long-context load to confirm, add automated circuit-breaker to evict when frag_ratio > 0.6.
- Owners: Samir K (lead), Maya L (on-call), Alex P (runtime).

Ops-OnCall: handing off to NightOnCall at 13:00 UTC. Please continue monitoring and update status page as needed. :white_check_mark:

NightOnCall: acknowledged - will maintain monitoring and escalate if fragmentation increases. Saved eviction job logs and canary metrics to incident INC-2026-0421.

Maya L: uploaded diagnostics, time-series graphs, and collected logs to incident ticket. Will write postmortem with timeline and recommended test coverage.

Alex P: thanks team. Postmortem to include PR ids, deploy timeline, and recommended guardrails (auto-evict on frag_ratio > 0.6, add rotation race integration tests). Closing live mitigation after an additional 45 minutes of clean metrics.

incident-bot: INC-2026-0421 status updated -> mitigated; monitoring. Handoff recorded."
